citations.quote: if $X\ne\varnothing$ and $n\ge1$ this is a compact Hausdorff second-countable smooth complex manifold of complex dimension $n$ ([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]); if $n=0$ it is the finite discrete set $X(\mathbb C)$ with its unique complex structure in the convention of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]; and if $X=\varnothing$ then $X^{\mathrm{an}}=\varnothing$. Every standard smooth algebraic chart of $X$ becomes a holomorphic chart of $X^{\mathrm{an}}$, and every morphism of smooth complex schemes $X\to Y$ induces a holomorphic map $X^{\mathrm{an}}\to Y^{\mathrm{an}}$. Moreover, for every ample invertible sheaf $A$ on $X$ there is a smooth positive closed real $(1,1)$-form $\eta_A$ on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ whose de Rham class is the real image of the topological first Chern class $c_1(A):=c_1(A^{\mathrm{an}})\in H^2(X^{\mathrm{an}};\mathbb Z)$: $$J_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}[\eta_A]=\rho_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}\bigl(c_1(A)\bigr),$$

Assume AC. For a compact Kähler manifold $X$ in the sense of [[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], every de Rham class has a unique smooth harmonic representative and $$H^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}H^{p,q}(X),\qquad \overline{H^{p,q}(X)}=H^{q,p}(X).$$ Here $H^{p,q}(X)$ is precisely the set of classes with a $d$-closed smooth representative of type $(p,q)$, so the decomposition is independent of the Kähler metric. Writing $\Omega_X^p$ for the sheaf of holomorphic $p$-forms (the kernel of $\bar\partial$ on the sheaf $\mathcal A^{p,0}$ of smooth $(p,0)$-forms), $H^{p,q}(X)$ is isomorphic to $H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$, the sheaf cohomology of [[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]. The Hodge filtration $F^a=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}H^{p,k-p}$ of $H^k(X;\mathbb C)$ equals the filtration induced by the holomorphic-degree filtration of the de Rham complex, whose spectral sequence has $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$ and degenerates at $E_1$. Pullback by holomorphic maps of compact Kähler manifolds and cup product preserve Hodge type, so $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)$ is a functorial rational pure Hodge structure.

For a compact smooth manifold $X$, the natural coefficient maps induce isomorphisms $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}F\cong H^k(X;F)$ for every characteristic-zero field $F$, finite-dimensional in each degree. For $F=\mathbb R,\mathbb C$ these identify singular cohomology with the real or complex de Rham cohomology. They preserve cup products and are natural for maps between such manifolds. No ordered-field or positivity structure is asserted for a general $F$.

Primitive cohomology is $P^k=\{a\in H^k(X;\mathbb R):\text{the harmonic representative of }a\text{ lies in }\ker\Lambda\}$, and for $0\le k\le n$ one has $P^k=\ker\bigl(L^{n-k+1}:H^k(X;\mathbb R)\to H^{2n-k+2}(X;\mathbb R)\bigr)$; for every $k$, $$H^k(X;\mathbb R)=\bigoplus_{r\ge\max(0,k-n)}L^rP^{k-2r},$$ and a class of type $(p,q)$ has primitive components of type $(p-r,q-r)$.

If $[\omega]=\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, then $Q_k$ is a rational polarization of $P^k$, and full $H^k$ is polarized by the orthogonal direct sum form $S_k$ that on $L^rP^{k-2r}$ is $(-1)^rQ_k$, equivalently $S_k(L^ru,L^rv)=Q_{k-2r}(u,v)$ for $u,v\in P^{k-2r}$; degrees $k>n$ are polarized by transporting the polarization of $H^{2n-k}$ along $L^{k-n}$, with Tate shift.

Then $Q|_U$ is a polarization of $U$, and $$V=U\oplus U^{\perp_Q},\qquad U^{\perp_Q}=\{x\in V:Q(x,U)=0\}$$ is an orthogonal direct sum of rational Hodge structures in which the complement is polarized. Every short exact sequence of polarizable rational pure Hodge structures of a fixed weight splits in the category of Hodge structures, and every polarizable rational pure Hodge structure is a finite direct sum of simple Hodge structures.

derivations.claim: The analytification is compact Kähler of dimension $n$ and $\ell$ is realized by a positive closed $(1,1)$-form, so it has type $(1,1)$; the Hodge theorem and the rational comparison make each $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)$ a finite-dimensional pure Hodge structure, functorial for holomorphic pullback with Hodge-type cup product.

Hard Lefschetz in degrees $\le n$ and its inverse reading $\ell^{k-n}$ in degrees $>n$ are isomorphisms, the Lefschetz decomposition and the type shift hold in every degree, and all of this data is rational at the rational class $\ell$.

The Hodge-Riemann positivity and sign-adjusted polarization hold on the primitive summands and on the full cohomology, the orthogonal-splitting lemma splits rational sub-Hodge structures, and the rational identities persist under characteristic-zero scalar extension; no supplier asserts the excluded relative or local-system statements.
